newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DOCdata sees strong profit growth.
newsitem.headline: DOCdata sees strong profit growth.

text.p: Dutch compact disc maker DOCdata NV said on Wednesday it saw net profit growth for full 1997 in line with its strong growth average of recent years.

Profits rose some 36 percent year-on-year in 1996 to almost 8 million guilders. Earlier today the firm reported a 60 percent net profit rise during the first six months of 1997 to 4.3 million guilders from 2.7 million in the same 1996 half.
"The interest burden during the second half of 1997 should be close to zero," DOCdata president Hans van Gerwen told Reuters in an interview.

DOCdata, which sought a bourse listing in Amsterdam and Nasdaq in May this year to finance future growth, saw total liabilities drop to 22.9 million guilders at the end of June 1997 compared to 86.2 million at the end of 1996, partly because it paid off all its subordinated loans.
DOCdata said it expected turnover to double in three years' time and it said it aimed for an annual growth in operating profit of at least 20 percent.
Organic growth should be between 20 to 25 percent annually, the firm said, adding it was also looking for acquisitions.
Operating profit grew by 37 percent in the first six months of 1997 to almost 7.6 million guilders.
"We will not give a precise forecast for the whole of 1997," Van Gerwen said, but added he saw no reason to expect that the earnings uptrend would not continue.
